title: Liberty Mutual posts US$2.6 billion quarter as cats drop, but core costs rise
full_text:
Liberty Mutual's second-quarter net income jumped 42.8% to US$2.634 billion from $1.845 billion a year earlier, but the gain had more to do with a quieter catastrophe quarter than any improvement in underlying loss costs.
CAT losses dropped 43.7% in Q2 to US$455 million, accounting for 4.2 combined ratio points versus 7.3 points a year ago. Over the first six months, catastrophe losses declined 61% to US$1.024 billion from US$2.629 billion.
The consolidated combined ratio improved to 86.4% in Q2 from 87.2%, and to 87.3% year to date from 91.9%. The underlying combined ratio, which strips out catastrophe losses and prior-year reserve development, widened 2.4 points to 84.5% in Q2, up from 84.1% in Q2 2025. That trajectory points to modest pressure on core loss costs even as headline results improved.
For brokers placing commercial and specialty risks, the most relevant split is between segments. Global Risk Solutions (GRS) net written premium rose 3.5% in Q2 to US$4.439 billion and 4.4% in the first half to US$9.393 billion. Within GRS, retention fell to 85.5% from 89.8% in Q1, and new business premium declined to US$894 million from US$1.06 billion. That metric points to some volume softening even as period NWP held up.
US Retail Markets (USRM), the segment covering personal and small commercial lines, posted a combined ratio of 82.3%, improving 2.9 points on lower catastrophe losses. Its NWP contracted 4.1% to US$6.627 billion, driven by lower average written premium per personal lines policy. Auto renewal pricing slowed to 0.5% from 4.5% a year earlier, with the aggregate USRM renewal rate falling to 1.2% from 5.5%. Personal lines retention improved, with auto retention recovering to 74% from 67.6%, suggesting brokers are holding business better as pricing pressure eases.
Total consolidated revenues rose 6% in Q2 to US$13.251 billion, with pre-tax operating income up 29.8% to US$3.259 billion. A large portion of the earnings improvement came from limited partnership income rather than underwriting. LP income more than doubled in Q2, up 107.3% to US$850 million from US$410 million a year ago, and up 88.7% to US$1.466 billion for the first half.
CEO Tim Sweeney attributed the result to "exceptional investment results from LMI across both traditional and alternative assets." The underlying pre-tax operating income before LP income was US$2.613 billion in Q2, down 2% year over year, with the year-to-date figure also slightly lower at US$5.204 billion versus US$5.378 billion.
Total equity reached US$44.071 billion at June 30, up 10.5% from US$39.887 billion at year-end 2025. Cash flow from operating activities was US$1.886 billion for the quarter, up 6.9%. "With the strongest balance sheet in our history, we are well positioned to pursue profitable growth, and to serve our policyholders with the financial strength and flexibility required over the long term," Sweeney said.
Liberty Mutual also disclosed that on July 30, it received a favourable arbitration award of US$1.570 billion against the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. The award has not been recorded in the financial statements for the period ended June 30, consistent with accounting rules on gain contingencies. Collection involves additional procedural steps.
